## Purpose
`ProjectDetail.tsx` and `SessionDetail.tsx` are the subproject's drill-in route components, each reached via a `:id`-style route param through `useParams`. Both resolve their entity from existing client state (a `useQuery`/`queryClient` cache lookup or a store selector) rather than re-fetching a bespoke "detail" endpoint, and both render an explicit "no project selected" / "not found" `EmptyState` branch before the real content — a detail page never assumes its dependencies are present.

## Convention
Folder: apps/dashboard/src/pages/** · Extension: .tsx · Files of this role in this subproject: 2
Named `export function <Noun>Detail()`, taking no props (route-driven). The id comes from `useParams<{ id: string }>()`; `SessionDetail.tsx` decodes it with `decodeURIComponent` because session ids can contain path-unsafe characters. Both open with `<PageSurface>` → `<EditorialBand eyebrow=... title=... subtitle=...>` as the header, with the `eyebrow` a `<Link>` back to the parent list route. Both guard on the required upstream state (`projectsRoot`, `project`) with an early-return `EmptyState`/error branch BEFORE the main render, and hooks that must obey Rules of Hooks (like `useActiveProjectName`) are called unconditionally above that guard, never after it.

## How to apply
A new `<Noun>Detail` page lives in `src/pages/<Noun>Detail.tsx`, wired to a `/<noun>s/:id` route. Resolve the entity from the already-loaded list query/store rather than adding a new single-entity backend command unless the detail view genuinely needs richer data (as `SessionDetail` does via `<ExecutionTrace>`). Keep the `PageSurface`/`EditorialBand` header shape and the pre-render empty/error guard as the first two structural pieces.
